The Al0.3Si0.3 alloy exhibits a distinct FCC and body-centered cubic (BCC) duplex structure
One size, averaging 5.6 μ m with a volume fraction of 10.1 %, is identified as the B2 phase rich in Ni and Al
The other BCC phase, with an average size of 584 nm and a volume fraction of 4.5 %, initially believed to be a Cr-rich BCC phase, is later confirmed as a B2 phase rich in Ni and Al elements

a smaller B2 phase was also detected within the FCC grains, as depicted in Fig. 2 (e) and highlighted by selected area electron diffraction (SAED) in Fig. 2 (e2). This smaller B2 phase has a composition rich in Ni and Al, as confirmed from Fig. 9 (b), with an average grain size of 248 nm and a volume fraction of 3.2 %.
The alloy matrix is characterized by fine equiaxed grains without a discernible texture, with an average grain size of 3.2 μ m.
